weekly-progress.name: Weekly Progress
weekly-progress.summary: Tight rhythm-of-business arc for weekly progress reports: objectives, achievements, progress, challenges, opportunities, recognition, plan, discussion, conclusion. Designed for fifteen-to-thirty-minute team check-ins, not deep dives.

beats.name: Opening
beats.description: Open with the initiative name, the date, and the one-line headline for the week. Frame the meeting in fifteen seconds so the rest of the time is content.

beats.name: Objectives
beats.description: State what the team set out to do this week. Specific, measurable. The audience should be able to read this slide alone and know what 'on track' would mean.

beats.name: Achievements
beats.description: Celebrate the week's wins. Concrete, attributable, dated. Brevity here — the meeting is for what's next, not a victory lap.

beats.name: Overall Progress
beats.description: Evaluate performance against the objectives. Use a simple status indicator (green/yellow/red) plus the leading metric. Help the audience scan the state in seconds.

beats.name: Challenges
beats.description: Address what's hard right now: blockers, slipping items, surfaced risks. Tie each challenge to either an owner working it or a discussion you want this week.

beats.name: Opportunities for Improvement
beats.description: Surface where the team can level up. Process tweaks, tooling needs, ways of working. Improvement opportunities should feel like seeds, not corrections.

beats.name: Highlights & Recognition
beats.description: Recognize specific contributions by name. Recognition belongs in the deck, not just in the meeting — written acknowledgment travels further than verbal.

beats.name: Goals Next Week
beats.description: Plan the week ahead with three to five specific goals. Each should be small enough to finish, large enough to matter, and clearly owned.

beats.name: Discussion & Feedback
beats.description: Open the floor with two or three prompts — decisions you need, opinions you want, blockers you'd like cleared. End the recap actively.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Close with one line that motivates the team into the next week. Echo the headline so the meeting feels closed.

sales.name: Sales
sales.summary: Sales team or prospective customers focused on product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI justification.
sales.description: Sales teams and prospective customers weighing product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI. Put customer success stories first, back claims with visual proof points, state the value proposition plainly, and close on a strong call to action. Moderate chart density; 15-25 slides.

board.name: Board of Directors
board.summary: Directors with fiduciary responsibility who balance oversight, advice, and approval.
board.description: The board is governance-first. They want a complete picture: financial health, key metrics, functional updates, risks, and forward-looking topics. Surface bad news honestly — under-disclosure erodes trust faster than the problems themselves. Bring specific asks that turn the meeting into a working session rather than a recital.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

noto-sans-arabic.name: Noto Sans Arabic
noto-sans-arabic.description: Noto Sans Arabic is a sans serif OPF font scheme for complex script presentations, using Noto Naskh Arabic for both headings and body text.

courier-new.name: Courier New
courier-new.description: Courier New is a monospace OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Courier New for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

pastel-red.name: Pastel Red
pastel-red.summary: Soft red and blue accents for approachable consumer stories.
pastel-red.description: A pastel red scheme with warm neutrals and blue support, suited to friendly, human-centered decks.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
